content.text: targeting the anagen hair follicles (scalp MC)
▪︎benign; nonscarring hair loss in hair-bearing areas throughout body
▪︎unknown cause; hypothesized autoimmune in persons w/ genetic predispositions
▪︎hair loss = 1 patch (MC) or multiple; scalp = MC area, then beard, eyebrows, extremities; can affect >1 area at once
▪︎alopecia universalis = complete hair loss on all hair-bearing areas
▪︎also assoc: atopic dermatitis, vitiligo, Down syndrome, psych d/os (eg anxiety, depression); high stress (esp stressors in the 6 mo before onset)
that develop over a period of wks (painless & ⍉pruritic)
▪︎typically aSx; some pts may feel burning or itching in affected areas
: short hairs broken off a few mm from the scalp w/ tapering near the prox hair shaft (exclamation point appearance) @ the margins of the patches
-in some cases, hair loss may be diffuse
-hair regrowth may occur (fine white hair regrowth)
no erythema, inflam, or scarring seen
: pitting ~30%, nail fissuring, trachyonychia (roughening of the nail plate)
: definitive dx – peribulbar lymphocytic inflam infiltrates surrounding the follicles
▪︎(+) hair pull test: grasp ~40–60 hairs, apply steady traction while sliding along the hair — ⊕ if >10% pulled
; may be observed in mild cases
▪︎also: immunotherapy (squaric acid dibutylester), topical anthralin, topical minoxidil, topical or systemic psoralen + UVA
Genetically predetermined progress loss of the terminal hairs on the scalp in a characteristic distribution (pattern)
MC type of hair loss in men & women
; gradual in onset & USU occurs after puberty
; activate of the androgen-r shortens the anagen (growth phase) in the norm hair growth cycle
: begins as bitemporal thinning of the frontal scalp then involves the vertex
: thinning of the hair b/n the frontal & vertex of the scalp w/o affecting the frontal hairline
: widens blood vessels, allowing more blood, O2, & nutrients to promote the anagen (growth) phase
: androgen inhibitor (inhibits conversions of testosterone to DHT)
: ↓ libido, sexual or ejaculatory dysfun, ↑ risk of high-grade prostate CA,
•candida albicans (more likely to affect fingernails) & ⍉dermatophyte molds
: ↑ age, tinea pedis (incl close contacts), psoriasis, occlusive shoes, immunodeficiency

Mgnt initiated if KOH/PAS + while waiting for cultures
Infect of the lat & prox nail folds <6wks
▪︎begins as superficial cellulitis + can progress to an abscess
▪︎chronic: inflammatory disorder of the nail folds; redness, tenderness + swelling >6wks (tx corticosteroids ± antifungals)
: MC occurs after penetrating skin trauma (dishwashing, biting nails, cuticle damage during manicures, ingrown nails)
Painful, red, swollen area around the prox or lat nail folds @ the cuticle
▪︎gram stain or cx can identify the bacterium
▪︎extensive cellulitis, DM, PVD, immunocompromised, or refractory to topical abx → may require oral abx
▪︎I&D → immediate relief of Sx; typically ⍉oral abx after I&D unless severe or immunocompromised
▪︎complications (esp immunocompromised): abscess, cellulitis + erysipelas, deep hand infections (felon (pulp-space abscess), pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, tendon-sheath phlegmon), osteomyelitis
